definitions.explanation: Outward display or embellishment that lacks substance; putting on a showy front to conceal the reality underneath.

examples.japanese: {虚飾|きょしょく}を{捨|す}てる。
{虚飾|きょしょく}のない{生|い}き{方|かた}がしたい。
examples.english: I want to live without pretense.

examples.japanese: {虚飾|きょしょく}に{満|み}ちた{社会|しゃかい}に{疲|つか}れて、{田舎|いなか}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した。
examples.english: Tired of a society full of false show, I moved to the countryside.

notes:
A compound of {虚|きょ} (empty, vain) and {飾|しょく} (decoration, adornment). Describes the negative quality of ornamenting or embellishing to hide a lack of substance. Often used in literary and critical contexts.

USAGE:
Frequently appears in the negative — {虚飾|きょしょく}のない (without pretense) and {虚飾|きょしょく}を{排|はい}する (to reject ostentation) — to praise honesty and simplicity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虚飾|きょしょく}を{捨|す}てる — to cast off pretense
- {虚飾|きょしょく}のない — without pretense, honest
- {虚飾|きょしょく}に{満|み}ちた — full of false show
- {虚飾|きょしょく}を{排|はい}する — to reject ostentation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見栄|みえ} — vanity, showing off; more everyday and personal, while {虚飾|きょしょく} is broader and more literary
- {虚栄|きょえい} — vanity; focuses on the desire for admiration, while {虚飾|きょしょく} emphasizes the outward display itself
